pr_title: sql: wait for local orchestrator during ALTER TENANT SERVICE
pr_body:
Similar to SET CLUSTER SETTING, this waits for the local server orcehstrator to start or stop a server before returning from an ALTER TENANT command that modifies the service_mode.

As a result, you can no longer issue ALTER TENANT inside anything but an implicit transaction.

Epic: none

Fixes #112554
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/115094)

Hrm. Unfortunately, one of the points of this was to resolve an issue we saw during some tests in which we are still writing to the tenant after the tenant service has stopped. But this doesn't seem to have done the trick...
We now do this for `STOP`. If we want to do it for `START` as well the code would look pretty different.

issue_context.title: streamingccl: TestTenantStreamingFailback timed out
comments:
From the stack trace, it looks like the problem was that we were waiting to shut down:

```
time.Sleep(0x4c4b40)
	GOROOT/src/runtime/time.go:195 +0x135
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/util/stop.(*Stopper).Quiesce(0xc0033112c0, {0xd8452b0?, 0xc0001ba008})
	github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/util/stop/stopper.go:604 +0x2c6
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/util/stop.(*Stopper).Stop(0xc0033112c0, {0xd8452b0, 0xc0001ba008})
	github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/util/stop/stopper.go:543 +0x14d
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/ccl/streamingccl/streamingest.TestTenantStreamingFailback(0xc003708000)
	github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/ccl/streamingccl/streamingest/stream_ingestion_job_test.go:302 +0x237b

	GOROOT/src/testing/testing.go:1576 +0x217
created by testing.(*T).Run
	GOROOT/src/testing/testing.go:1629 +0x806
```

But it isn't clear to me from the stacks what is holding up shutdown.

Intriguing. I'll note that I was recently looking at a test failure (on 23.1) where shutdown was stuck potentially by a gc finalizer that we could not observe in the stacks in the artifacts. In other words, in that test failure,[ quiescing succeeded](https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C054X9T82AU/p1697652598232599?thread_ts=1697647577.353129&cid=C054X9T82AU).
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/112469#issuecomment-1768749191
I'm going to err on the side of closing this out. If we see it again or get dinged for it we can revisit. The test history over the past 3-4 days looks decently green

It flaked (no timeout) here on the `master` branch: https://teamcity.cockroachdb.com/buildConfiguration/Cockroach_BazelEssentialCi/12491945?hideProblemsFromDependencies=false&hideTestsFromDependencies=false&expandBuildChangesSection=true&expandBuildProblemsSection=true&expandBuildTestsSection=true

```
    stream_ingestion_job_test.go:744: tenant "g" is still accepting connections
    stream_ingestion_job_test.go:747: tenant "g" is not accepting connections
    stream_ingestion_job_test.go:285: starting replication f->g
    stream_ingestion_job_test.go:289: waiting for g@1699036101656260960.0000000000
    stream_ingestion_job_test.go:168:
          Error Trace:  github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/ccl/streamingccl/streamingest/stream_ingestion_job_test.go:168
                              github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/ccl/streamingccl/streamingest/stream_ingestion_job_test.go:299
          Error:        Not equal:
                        expected: 4438609793771831563
                        actual  : -5645868812438106101
          Test:         TestTenantStreamingFailback
          Messages:     fingerprint mismatch at 1699036101656260960.0000000000
```
Yikes. A checksum mismatch. Thanks for reporting this!

From reading the logs, I think this is a race in the test. Namely, we currently don't have a great way to make sure the tenant is actually shut down. From the logs, it appears that the tenant may have still been up at the point that we tried to reset its timestamp.
I'm demoting this from GA blocker to p-2 since tailback isn't officially supported in 23.2 anyway and this is just a race condition that a runbook could handle with a delay.
Fixed in master and unsupported in 23.2. Closing. If this recurs, we'll delete the 23.2 test.

review_comments: nit: could it be clearer to call this a `ServerChecker` instead of a `ServerOrchestrator`, which may imply an ability to modify state?
er, maybe you're trying to relate this interface to the private `serverOrchestrator` interface  in the server package? Are you hoping to migrate that private interface into this new package?
Yeah, originally I was going to expose more functionality but then I realized I only needed this single function.
why retry on all other errors? I don't see how `CheckRunningServer` could return anything other than `ErrTenantServerNotReady` and `ErrNoTenantServerRunning`.
This isn't retrying any other error, it is returning any other error, which we don't expect currently.
shouldn't we only wait if `serverorchestrator.ErrTenantServerNotReady` returns?
No, we'll get the other error if the service orchestrator hasn't yet even seen the service mode update  yet.
